knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.3.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly defines E[Y|X=x]?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the meaning and construction of conditional expectation.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Conditional expectation averages Y using its distribution after fixing X=x, so its value can vary with x.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Expected Y under Y|X=x; a function of x and generally different from E[Y].
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Replacing the conditional mean with the unconditional mean or a single joint cell.

choices.label: E[Y|X=x] is the expected value of Y under the conditional distribution of Y given X=x. As x varies it is a function of x, and it need not equal E[Y].
E[Y|X=x] is always the unconditional mean E[Y] because expectation removes all conditioning information.
E[Y|X=x] is the joint probability P(X=x,Y=y) evaluated at the largest y.
Conditional expectation is a fixed constant that cannot depend on the value x.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.3.1
knowledge_checks.body: Compute the conditional mean from the joint PMF.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Normalise the X=1 row, then average Y under that conditional distribution.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Using E[Y] or the unnormalised joint cell instead of the conditional distribution.

choices.label: E[Y|X=1]=E[Y]=0.60 because conditioning does not change an expectation.
E[Y|X=1]=0.40 because the joint cell P(1,1) needs no normalisation.
E[Y|X=1]=0.70 because the marginal P(X=1) is itself the conditional mean of Y.
